entries.title: Isaiah 56:1
segments:
. THE PREPARATION NEEDED ON THE PART OF THOSE WHO WISH TO BE ADMITTED TO THE KINGDOM OF GOD. 
 
    1. judgment--equity. John the Baptist preached similarly a return to righteousness, as needed to prepare men for Messiah's first coming (
). So it shall be before the second coming (

). 
 
    near to come-- (
), also as to the second coming (

). 
 
    righteousness--answering to "salvation" in the parallel clause; therefore it means righteousness which bringeth salvation (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:2
segments:
). 
 
    the man--Hebrew, enosh, "a man in humble life," in contradistinction to Hebrew, ish, "one of high rank." Even the humblest, as "the stranger" and "the eunuch" (

), are admissible to these privileges. 
 
    this ... it--what follows: "keeping the Sabbath," &c. (
). A proof that the Sabbath, in the spirit of its obligation, was to be binding under the Gospel (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:3
segments: 3. God welcomes all believers, without distinction of persons, under the new economy (

). 
 
    joined ... to ... Lord-- (

). "Proselytes." 
 
    separated--Proselytes from the Gentiles were not admitted to the same privileges as native Israelites. This barrier between Jews and Gentiles was to be broken down (

). 
 
    eunuch-- (

, &c.). Eunuchs were chamberlains over harems, or court ministers in general. 
 
    dry tree--barren (compare
); not admissible into the congregation of Israel (
). Under the Gospel the eunuch and stranger should be released from religious and civil disabilities.

entries.title: Isaiah 56:4
segments:
4. please me--sacrifice their own pleasure to mine. 
 
    take hold--so "layeth hold" (see on

entries.title: Isaiah 56:5
segments: 5. in mine house--the temple, the emblem of the Church (
). They shall no longer be confined as proselytes were, to the outer court, but shall be admitted "into the holiest" (
), I will give him a more lasting name than that of being father of sons and daughters (regarded as a high honor among the Hebrews) (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:6
segments: 6. join ... Lord-- (
). Conditions of admission to the privileges of adoption.

entries.title: Isaiah 56:7
segments: 7. Even them-- (

). 
 
    to my holy mountain--Jerusalem, the seat of the Lord's throne in His coming kingdom (

). 
 
    joyful-- (

). 
 
    burnt offerings ... sacrifices--spiritual, of which the literal were types (

). 
 
    accepted-- (

). 
 
    altar-- (

), spiritually, the Cross of Christ, which sanctifies our sacrifices of prayer and praise. 
 
    house ... for all people--or rather, "peoples." No longer restricted to one favored people (
). To be fully realized at the second coming (
). No longer literal, but spiritual sacrifice, namely, "prayer" shall be offered (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:8
segments: 8. Jehovah will not only restore the scattered outcasts of Israel (

) to their own land, but "will gather others ('strangers') to him (Israel), besides those gathered" (Margin, "to his gathered"; that is, in addition to the Israelites collected from their dispersion), (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:9
segments: 9. beasts--Gentile idolatrous nations hostile to the Jews, summoned by God to chastise them (
): the Chaldeans and subsequently the Romans. The mention of the "outcasts of Israel" (
) brings in view the outcasting, caused by the sins of their rulers (

). 
 
    to devour--namely, Israel.

entries.title: Isaiah 56:10
segments: 10. His watchmen--Israel's spiritual leaders (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:11
segments: 11. greedy--literally, "strong" (that is, insatiable) in appetite (

). 
 
    cannot understand--unable to comprehend the wants of the people, spiritually: so

, "cannot bark." 
 
    look to ... own way--that is, their own selfish interests; not to the spiritual welfare of the people (

). 
 
    from his quarter--rather, "from the highest to the lowest" [LOWTH]. "From his quarter"; that is, from one end to the other of them, one and all (

entries.title: Isaiah 56:12
segments: 12. fetch wine--language of the national teachers challenging one another to drink. BARNES translates, "I will take another cup" (

). 
 
    to-morrow, &c.--Their self-indulgence was habitual and intentional: not merely they drink, but they mean to continue so.
